title: Advance release candidate past reserved v0.5.45
outOfScope: Deleting, moving, publishing, or reusing the immutable v0.5.45 tag or its Draft Release.
Changing the public v0.5.42 release projection without new published provider evidence.
Lowering release, coverage, or Hosted CI requirements.

sources.reason: Canonical release state records reserved and unavailable semantic versions.
Unpublished candidate projection that must advance past the reserved v0.5.45 tag.
Failed v0.5.45 publication created an immutable tag and retained Draft Release evidence.
Authoritative documentation for reserved-version and next-patch candidate rules.

riskAssessment.reason: Release-candidate metadata can misrepresent provider state or attempt to reuse a reserved semantic version.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized continuous release correction; external publication remains a later, separately verified action.

preReviewWarnings: Review the v0.5.45 unavailable-record evidence and exact next-patch progression to v0.5.46.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: v0.5.45 is recorded as an unavailable reserved version with the failed publication and retained Draft Release as evidence.
next-release.json and canonical release-state.json name v0.5.46 as the single unpublished candidate, exactly one patch above the highest reserved version.
Candidate supply-chain baselines and both release-state metadata digests are regenerated through authoritative generators, not hand-edited.
Regression coverage proves the repository candidate cannot reuse v0.5.45 and must remain v0.5.46 until an actual publication changes the public projection.
Release state, source-bound documentation evidence, all required governance gates, and Hosted CI remain enforced.
guidelines: Do not reuse, delete, move, or publish a reserved semantic version as corrective cleanup.
Use authoritative generators for derived supply-chain evidence and synchronize every affected canonical metadata digest.
Do not lower release, coverage, or Hosted CI requirements to advance a candidate.

intent.problem: The failed v0.5.45 publication reserved an immutable tag and retains a Draft Release. The candidate record still names v0.5.45, which violates the canonical next-patch rule and would cause future release retries to repeat the invalid version.
constraints: Preserve v0.5.45 and its Draft Release as failure evidence; do not mutate provider state in this Work Item.
Advance to exactly v0.5.46, not a skipped or reused semantic version.
Regenerate supply-chain evidence through repository generators and keep the public v0.5.42 projection unchanged.
Retain required governance gates and independent Hosted CI while omitting only the user-authorized redundant local quality suite.
intent.rationale: Making the reserved-version rule executable in canonical metadata prevents the next release workflow from retrying a semantically unavailable tag.

verification.reason: Temporary user-authorized focused-verification exception; it does not waive governance gates or full Hosted CI.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: The user authorized continuous release correction, PR, merge, Hosted verification, and final release continuation.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff and restore related tests and docs.
rawUserRequest: Continue the approved release plan. Preserve failed v0.5.45 evidence and advance the candidate instead of reusing a reserved version.

declaredIntent.summary: Advance the candidate to v0.5.46 after v0.5.45 became a reserved, unavailable tag.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An immutable v0.5.45 tag and a retained Draft Release exist after failed publication.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Canonical state records v0.5.45 as unavailable/reserved and never offers it as the next candidate.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Release-state regression test, metadata consistency checks, and provider facts.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: The successor candidate must preserve the v0.5.42 public projection while advancing exactly one patch after the highest reserved version.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Only next-release.json and release-state.json name v0.5.46; candidate evidence is regenerated and Hosted CI remains required.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Focused release metadata tests, generator checks, governance gates, and Hosted CI.
